item.description: The company said Claude leads 26 percent of its research and development, an indicator of progress toward AI that builds itself without human help.

item.title: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. says Americans worried about vaccines have a ‘friend at the White House’
item.description: The health secretary’s remarks before the anti-vaccine group he founded came in the midst of the nation’s worst measles outbreak in 35 years and included claims that medical experts say are misleading.

item.title: Why probiotics don’t usually help your gut — and what to do instead
item.description: Probiotics use has climbed in recent years. But fiber-rich plants, not supplements, are the best fuel for your gut microbiome, writes columnist Anahad O’Connor.

item.description: The fiasco of this week’s closure reveals the truth of President Donald Trump’s motivations — and what the arts community stands to lose.

item.title: A baby died in his care. He has spent years trying to clear his name.
item.description: A judge is weighing Curtis Ryan Morris’s case years after his conviction in the 2012 death of a 3-month-old infant in his care. His legal team says the jury never saw key evidence.

item.title: Trump withdraws his nominee to lead ICE amid mounting signs Lance Schroyer would face resistance in Senate
item.description: The Senate has not confirmed an ICE director in over a decade. Trump selected Schroyer, a former Oklahoma Highway Patrol major and Marine, for the role less than three months ago.

item.title: Photo of Trump with printout appearing to refer to potential Kennedy Center demolition is cited as evidence in new court filing
item.description: The image surfaced hours after the president warned that the performing arts venue could eventually be “ripped down” without his intervention. Lawyers for Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-Ohio), a Kennedy Center trustee challenging Trump’s transformation of the institution, filed a copy in federal court Thursday.

item.title: Former youth minister Jeff Taylor is indicted on sex abuse charges after FBI probe
item.description: Taylor worked at one of the most prominent churches in Northern Virginia, Falls Church Episcopal, in the 1990s and early 2000s. He has been arrested and charged with coercing and trying to coerce three minors into sexual activity, according to a federal grand jury indictment.

item.title: Trump wants U.S. citizens? So give them to him.
item.description: Democrats need a pro-citizenship approach to counter Trump’s census plan.

item.description: The forecast of economic impacts beyond November’s midterms contrast with the Trump administration’s optimistic messaging.

item.description: The Federal Reserve raised rates in an effort to fight stubborn inflation, but that won’t mean the mortgage rate you’ve been eyeing will suddenly shoot up.

item.title: 6 resistance band exercises for healthy aging and better mobility
item.description: The simple, joint-friendly workout can build strength as effectively as gym equipment — and the bands fit right in your bag.

item.title: Afghan man convicted of terrorism is sentenced to 20 years in prison for role in 2021 Kabul airport bombing
item.description: Mohammad Sharifullah was the only person convicted in connection with the attack at Kabul airport’s Abbey Gate during the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan. The jury convicted Sharifullah of helping ISIS leaders that day but did not find that the prosecution had sufficiently proved that the man’s role in the attack directly resulted in the deaths of 13 U.S. service members.

item.title: Trump’s arch will harm dozens of historic sites but must proceed, federal officials say
item.description: National Park Service officials acknowledge that, if built as planned, President Donald Trump’s triumphal arch would adversely affect Arlington National Cemetery, the Lincoln Memorial and several dozen other historic sites, but they say the project must move forward, according to an NPS document and emails obtained by The Washington Post.

item.title: Lawmaker requests emergency hearing on Kennedy Center closure, escalating fight over Trump’s transformation of the venue
item.description: The challenge from Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-Ohio), a Kennedy Center trustee who has repeatedly challenged the president in court, puts the question of the Kennedy Center’s physical future back before U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper barely 24 hours after he blocked another attempt to put President Donald Trump’s name on the building.

item.title: Fed raises interest rates by quarter point to tackle inflation, its first increase in more than 3 years
item.description: Even as President Donald Trump has called on the Federal Reserve to lower rates, Fed officials chose to increase its benchmark rate, hiking the cost of borrowing among banks, which will increase what millions of households and businesses pay to borrow, including credit cards and other loans.

item.title: Measles surge will be administration’s ‘terrible legacy,’ says Bill Cassidy, top Republican on Senate health committee
item.description: During the hearing for three key administration nominees, Trump’s surgeon general pick, Nicole Saphier, called a combined measles, mumps and rubella vaccine “our greatest tool for combating measles infections.”

item.title: Trump administration moving ahead with signs outside Smithsonian museum as part of effort to reshape how U.S. history is presented
item.description: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said about a dozen signs complying with President Donald Trump’s order would be installed outside the National Museum of American History. They would alert visitors to what the White House has called ideological bias in exhibits.

item.title: The restaurant was hosting a noisy event. Should it have warned me? Our food critic is taking questions.
item.description: Washington Post food critic Elazar Sontag entertains your restaurant questions, rants and raves.

item.title: GOP candidates are largely ignoring Trump’s midterm advice, Post analysis shows
item.description: A review of over a million social media posts reveals that Republicans haven’t heeded the president’s call to act like he’s on the ballot and promise $5,000 payouts. They’re sticking to their own messages, not Trump’s, as they navigate an increasingly difficult political landscape.

item.title: Lead you absorbed as a child reemerges in your blood as you age and may cause dementia, columnist Michael J. Coren writes
item.description: Americans born between 1951 and 1980 are invisibly scarred by lead exposure that embedded the toxic metal into their bones.

item.title: FBI Director Patel defends firing of numerous agents, declines to say whether bureau personnel will be sent to polling stations
item.description: In a hearing before a Senate panel, Kash Patel faced sharp questions from lawmakers about the dismissals, saying he was fighting the “weaponization” of law enforcement at the bureau.

item.title: This surgery can prevent a deadly cancer. Women need to know it’s an option.
item.description: There is no effective screening for ovarian cancer, but this procedure can help prevent it.

item.title: Kennedy Center board votes to close the performing arts venue
item.description: Administrators had warned that an immediate closure was necessary to avoid endangering people’s lives, days after a section of ceiling plaster collapsed in the center’s Grand Foyer. Hours earlier Tuesday, a judge had blocked efforts to add President Donald Trump’s name to the venue building again.

item.title: Trump’s planned sale of controversial bombs to Israel is largest in years
item.description: The pending transfer of the 2,000-pound munition, involved in scores of incidents resulting in civilian casualties, sets up a potential litmus test for Democrats.

item.title: Judge bars Kennedy Center’s latest attempt to add Trump’s name to building
item.description: The decision comes as the institution’s board of trustees is set to consider a proposal to shut the building because of management concerns of fiscal collapse.

item.title: Nick Reiner will not face possibility of death penalty if convicted in the killing of his parents, prosecutor says
item.description: Reiner, 33, has pleaded not guilty in the fatal stabbings of his mother and his father, the acclaimed filmmaker Rob Reiner. If convicted, Reiner will face a maximum penalty of life in prison without the possibility of parole.

item.title: Trump slams Supreme Court justices he appointed over mail ballot ruling, portraying it as a personal betrayal
item.description: “These are not the people I interviewed to serve on the United States Supreme Court, they are merely a shell of their original selves,” the president wrote on social media, reacting to the court’s Monday night ruling that blocked his administration’s restrictions on mail ballots in the midterms.

item.title: David Petraeus: Putin can’t win what he can’t afford
item.description: Demonstrate military genius on an industrial scale and show Russia that time isn’t on its side.

item.title: ICE is quietly firing new hires. For one recruit, it was devastating.
item.description: Joseph Moore killed himself after learning ICE was going to fire him. Investigators had identified issues in his past that ex-officials say should have blocked his hiring.

item.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump’s sweeping mail ballot restrictions for midterm elections
item.description: The ruling, a major defeat for the president, leaves intact election procedures and prohibits changes that could have had significant impacts for millions of voters set to vote by mail in contests that will determine which party controls the House and Senate. In a brief order Monday evening, the majority did not explain its reasoning for leaving in place a lower court order blocking the administration’s plans intact.

item.title: The 78th Emmy Awards are set to begin, with “The Pitt,” “Hacks” and “Widow’s Bay” among the favorites. Follow our coverage.
item.description: In the drama division, “The Pitt” seems poised to win big for the second year in a row, with 12 major nominations (from a total of 25). In the comedy categories, newcomer “Widow’s Bay” is facing off against onetime champion “Hacks,” which set the record for the most nominations for a comedy series in a single year (a whopping 24) back in July.

item.title: McConnell returns to Senate, casting his first vote since suffering a fall in June
item.description: The Kentucky Republican made his first public appearance since he suffered the fall at home. He provided the deciding vote to advance the nomination of Matthew R. Byrne to a district court judgeship in Ohio.

item.title: I’m a doctor. Here’s why I wouldn’t get a full-body MRI scan.
item.description: Celebrities sing their praises, but I’m not convinced the average person needs or should spend their money on one, Netana Markovitz writes.

item.title: Safety net spending has surged. Where’s the money going?
item.description: Federal anti-poverty spending comes out to $35,000 a year for every person in poverty, the Editorial Board writes.

item.description: A vision revolving around space lasers is attracting serious investment as a way to help solve the world’s energy shortage.

item.title: Alligator Alcatraz detainees were put in small cages, DHS watchdog report finds
item.description: The Florida facility’s staff referred to the enclosures as “calming areas.” Investigators said their use at the immigration detention center violated federal standards and did not align with “standards for humane treatment.”
